# Rises a change makes on purpose: one per line, as
#   <benchmark name prefix> <unit> <most rise> <reason...>
# unit: allocs/op, read-B/op or readcalls/op, the most as a count; or
# B/op or ns/op, the most as a percentage ("160%") in place of the gate's
# 10% or 25%. A PR that adds a line says why in its description; the line
# goes again once the change is on main.
BenchmarkPlanVideoEdit ns/op 170% read-back check: the movie parsed twice (source and edited) to compare every value but those the edit sets
BenchmarkPlanVideoEdit B/op 140% read-back check: the two reads of the movie
BenchmarkPlanVideoEdit allocs/op 200 read-back check: the two reads of the movie
BenchmarkPlanVideoEdit read-B/op 250 read-back check: the edited movie's top-level boxes, read through the plan
BenchmarkPlanVideoEdit readcalls/op 16 read-back check: the top-level boxes of the source and the edited movie
